definition_en: Additional Authentication Data - data that is integrity protected but not encrypted

Devices that may be used by software running on Host processors to offload or perform any type of compute or I/O task. Examples of accelerators include programmable agents (e.g., GPU/GPGPU), fixed- function agents, or reconfigurable agents such as FPGAs.
Access Control Services as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Advanced Error Reporting as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Advanced Encryption Standard-Galois Counter Mode as defined in NIST* publication [AES-GCM]
Alternate Routing ID as defined in PCIe Base Specification.
ACPI Source Language as defined in ACPI Specification
Address Translation Services as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Process of providing a digital signature for a set of measurements from a device and verifying those signatures and measurements on a host.
Process of determining whether an entity is who or what it claims to be.
Base Address Register as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Base Bus Number as defined in ACPI Specification
Base Class Code as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Byte Enable as defined in PCIe Base Specification

Bias refers to coherence tracking of HDM-D* memory regions by the owning device to indicate that the host may have a cache copy. The Bias Flip is a process used to change the bias state that indicates the host has a cached copy of the line (Bias=Host) by invalidating the cache state for the corresponding address(es) in the host such that the device has exclusive access (Bias=Device).
BAR Indicator Register as defined in PCIe Base Specification
CXL Host Bridge Register Info as defined in ACPI Specification
Coherent Device Attribute Table, a table that describes performance characteristics of a CXL device or a CXL switch.
Compatible ID as defined in ACPI Specification
Context Key IDentifier passed in the protocol flit for identifying security keys utilized for memory encryption using TSP.
Component Measurement and Authentication as defined in PCIe Base Specification
As defined in PCIe Base Specification
Security model in which every device available to the TEE is presumed to be trusted by all TEEs in the system.
Corrected Volatile Memory Error, a corrected error associated with volatile memory.

Compute Express Link, a low-latency, high-bandwidth link that supports dynamic protocol muxing of coherency, memory access, and I/O protocols, thus enabling attachment of coherent accelerators or memory devices.
Agent coherency protocol that supports device caching of Host memory.
PCIe-based non-coherent I/O protocol with enhancements for accelerator support.
Memory access protocol that supports device-attached memory.
CXL device with a specific Class Code as defined in Section 8.1.12.1.
Device Coherency agent on the device that is responsible for resolving coherency with respect to device caches and managing Bias states.
Dual Host, Fabric Managed, Switch Attached SLD EP
Dual Host, Fabric Managed, Switch Attached MLD EP
Data Link Layer Packet as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Data Object Exchange as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Set of host ports and devices within a single coherent HPA space
Within the context of a single VH, an Edge Switch other than the Host ES.
Physical port that can be a root port or a downstream switch port or an RCH Downstream Port

Device Physical Address. DPA forms a device-scoped flat address space. An LD-FAM device presents a distinct DPA space per LD. A G-FAM device presents the same DPA space to all hosts. The CXL HDM decoders or GFD decoders map HPA into DPA space.
Downstream Port Containment as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Device Specific Method as defined in ACPI Specification
Device Security Manager. A logical entity in a device that can be admitted into the TCB for a TVM and enforces security policies on the device.
Device Scoped Memory Affinity Domain as defined in Coherent Device Attribute Table (CDAT) Specification
Device Scoped Memory Affinity Structure as defined in Coherent Device Attribute Table (CDAT) Specification
Device Tracked Requestor Cache State – The requestor cache coherency state tracked by the device.
Designated Vendor-Specific Extended Capability as defined in PCIe Base Specification
End Bad as defined in PCIe Base Specification
PBR downstream switch port that connects to a device (including a GFD) or an HBR USP
PBR switch port suitable for connecting to an RP, device, or HBR USP.
Within the context of a single VH, a PBR switch that contains one or more Edge Ports.
PBR upstream switch port that connects to a root port
Enhanced Downstream Port Control as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Electrical Idle Exit Ordered Set as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Electrical Idle Ordered Set as defined in PCIe Base Specification
EIOS Sequence as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Exclusive Restricted CXL Device (formerly known as CXL 1.1 only Device). eRCD is a CXL device component that can operate only in RCD mode.
Exclusive Restricted CXL Host (formerly known as CXL 1.1 only host). eRCH is a CXL host component that can operate only in RCD mode.
TE State ownership tracking where the state change occurs explicitly utilizing a TE State change message that is independent of each memory transaction.
PBR switch port that connects to another PBR switch port.

Fabric-Attached Memory. HDM within a Type 2 or Type 3 device that can be made accessible to multiple hosts concurrently. Each HDM region can either be pooled (dedicated to a single host) or shared (accessible concurrently by multiple hosts).
A flexible high-speed port that is configured to support either PCIe or CXL.
CXL protocol over a Flex Bus interconnect.
The Fabric Manager is an entity separate from the switch or host firmware that controls aspects of the system related to binding and management of pooled ports and devices.
Link that contains traffic from multiple VCSs or an unbound physical port.
As defined in PCIe Base Specification
Global FAM. Highly scalable form of FAM that is presented to hosts without using Logical Devices (LDs). Like LD-FAM, G-FAM presents HDM that can be pooled or shared.
HPA-to-DPA translation mechanism inside a GFD
Global Observation. This is used in the context of coherence protocol as a message to know when data is guaranteed to be observed by all agents in the coherence domain for either a read or a write.
Home Agent. This is the agent on the host that is responsible for resolving system wide coherency for a given address.
Link operating in a mode, where all flits are in HBR format

Host-managed Device Memory. Device-attached memory that is mapped to system coherent address space and accessible to the Host using standard write-back semantics. Memory located on a CXL device can be mapped as either HDM or PDM.
Host-only Coherent HDM region type. Used only for Type 3 Devices.
Device Coherent HDM region type. Used only for Type 2 devices that rely on CXL.cache to manage coherence with the host.
Device Coherent using Back-Invalidate HDM region type. Can be used by Type 2 devices or Type 3 devices.
Hardware ID as defined in ACPI Specification
Heterogeneous Memory Attribute Table as defined in ACPI Specification
Within the context of a single VH, the single Edge Switch connected to the RP.
As defined in PCIe Base Specification
Interleave Granularity in number of bytes
Within the context of a single VH, a PBR switch that forwards VH traffic but is not a Host ES or downstream ES.
I/O Memory Management Unit as defined in PCIe Base Specification
TE State ownership tracking where the state change occurs implicitly as part of executing each memory transaction.
Defined by TSP as a host or accelerator device that issues TSP requests.
Independent Power Manager to (Master) Power Manager, PM messages from the device to the host.
Inter-Switch Link. PBR link that connects Fabric Ports.
Logical Device. Entity that represents a CXL Endpoint that is bound to a VCS. An SLD contains one LD. An MLD contains multiple LDs.
FAM that is presented to hosts via Logical Devices (LDs).
CXL.cachemem link layer clock rate usually defined by the flit rate during normal operation.
Link Training and Status State Machine as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Message Authentication Code; also referred to as Authentication Tag or Integrity value.
Set of flits which are aggregated together for MAC computation.
Representation of firmware/software or configuration data on a device.
Memory Error Firmware Notification. An EFN that is used to report memory errors.
Set of DC blocks that can be accessed by the same set of requesters.
Repair function that replaces a portion of memory (the “spared memory”) with a portion of functional memory at that same DPA.
Modified, Exclusive, Shared, and Invalid cache coherence protocol

Multi-headed MLD. CXL component that contains multiple CXL ports, each presenting an MLD or SLD. The ports must correctly operate when connected to any combination of common or different hosts. The FM API is used to configure each LD as well as the overall MH-MLD. Currently, MH-MLDs are architected only for Type 3 LDs. MH-MLDs are considered a specialized type of MLD and, as such, are subject to all functional and behavioral requirements of MLDs.

Multi-headed SLD. CXL component that contains multiple CXL ports, each presenting an SLD. The ports must correctly operate when connected to any combination of common or different hosts. The FM API is used to configure each SLD as well as the overall MH-SLD. Currently, MH-SLDs are architected only for Type 3 LDs.

Multi-Logical Device. CXL component that contains multiple LDs, out of which one LD is reserved for configuration via the FM API, and each remaining LD is suitable for assignment to a different host. Currently MLDs are architected only for Type 3 LDs.
An MLD Port is one that has linked up with an MLD Component. The port is natively bound to an FM- owned PPB inside the switch.
Manually-operated Retention Latch as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Message Signaled Interrupt as defined in PCIe Base Specification
This is the maximum possible expected negotiated link width.
Optimized Buffer Flush/Fill as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Orthogonal Header Content as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Operating System Capabilities as defined in ACPI Specification
CKID memory encryption key configured for use with non-TEE data.
Operating System-directed configuration and Power Management as defined in ACPI Specification
Link where all flits are in PBR format
Switch that supports PBR and has PBR enabled
CRC-32 calculated on the flit plaintext content. Encrypted PCRC is used to provide robustness against hard and soft faults internal to the encryption and decryption engines.

Private Device memory. Device-attached memory that is not mapped to system address space or directly accessible to Host as cacheable memory. Memory located on PCIe devices is of this type. Memory located on a CXL device can be mapped as either PDM or HDM.
Peer device in the context of peer-to-peer (P2P) accesses between devices.

Device that retains content across power cycling. A CXL Memory device can advertise “Persistent Memory” capability as long as it supports the minimum set of requirements described in Section 8.2.10.9. The platform owns the final responsibility of determining whether a memory device can be used as Persistent Memory. This determination is beyond the scope of CXL specification.
Programming Interface as defined in PCIe Base Specification
(Master) Power Manager to Independent Power Manager, PM messages from the host to the device.
PCI-to-PCI Bridge inside a CXL switch that is FM-owned. The port connected to a PPB can be disconnected, or connected to a PCIe component or connected to a CXL component.
CMA/SPDM session established between the TSM or TSM RoT and the DSM. Utilized for configuring and locking the device and setting and clearing memory encryption keys using TSP.

QoS Throttling Group, the group of CXL.mem target resources that are throttled together in response to QoS telemetry (see Section 3.3.3). Each QTG is identified using a number that is known as QTG ID. QTG ID is a positive integer.
Set of memory devices on a channel that together execute a transaction.
Shorthand for a Device that is operating in RCD mode (formerly known as CXL 1.1 Device)

Restricted CXL Device mode (formerly known as CXL 1.1 mode). The CXL operating mode with a number of restrictions. These restrictions include lack of Hot-Plug support and 68B Flit mode being the only supported flit mode. See Section 9.11.1 for the complete list of these restrictions.
Root Complex Event Collector, collects errors from PCIe RCiEPs, as defined in PCIe Base Specification.
Restricted CXL Host. CXL Host that is operating in RCD mode (formerly known as CXL 1.1 Host).
Root Complex Register Block as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Requestor Cache State – The cache coherency state tracked by the host or initiator

The contents, states, or information are not defined at this time. Reserved register fields must be read only and must return 0 (all 0s for multi-bit fields) when read. Reserved encodings for register and packet fields must not be used. Any implementation dependent on a Reserved field value or encoding will result in an implementation that is not CXL-spec compliant. The functionality of such an implementation cannot be guaranteed in this or any future revision of this specification. Flit, Slot, and message reserved bits should be cleared to 0 by the sender and the receiver should ignore them.
Requester PID. In the context of a GFD, the SPID from an incoming request.
Root System Description Table as defined in ACPI Specification
Secondary Bus Reset as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Sub-Class Code as defined in PCIe Base Specification
One or more optional CMA/SPDM sessions established between a host entity and the DSM. Utilized for setting and clearing memory encryption keys using TSP.
Security model in which each TEE selects which devices it shall include in its TCB. The device trusted by one TEE may not be trusted by other TEEs within the system.
Entity that is sharing data with another entity.
Single Host, Direct Attached SLD EP
Single headed MLD. CXL component that contains a single CXL port, presenting an MLD.
Single Headed Single Logical Device CXL component that contains a single CXL port, presenting an SLD.
Single Host, Switch Attached SLD EP
Single Host, Fabric Managed, Switch Attached SLD EP
Signal used for device detection, configuration, and Hot-Plug in PCIe connectors, as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Enhanced I/O with additional protocol support.
Security Protocol and Data Model over Data Object Exchange as defined in PCIe Base Specification
System Resource Affinity Table as defined in ACPI Specification
Separate Reference Clocks with Independent Spread Spectrum Clocking as defined in PCIe Base Specification
Defined by TSP as a memory expander device that receives TSP requests.
Trusted Computing Base - refers to the set of hardware, software and/or firmware entities that security assurances depend upon
PCI-SIG-defined TEE Device Interface Security Protocol
TEE or non-TEE intent of a memory request from an initiator defined by the opcodes utilized in the transaction.
TEE Exclusive State maintained by the device for each page or cacheline to enforce access control.
Transaction Layer Packet as defined in PCIe Base Specification
TEE Security Manager. Logical entity within a host processor that is the TCB for a TVM and enforces security policies on the host.
TEE Security Manager Root of Trust. The entity on the host that establishes the CMA/SPDM PrimarySession.
CXL-defined TEE Security Protocol. The collection of requirements and interfaces that allow memory devices to be utilized for confidential computing.
TEE Virtual Machine. A TEE that has the property of a virtual machine. A TVM does not need to trust the hypervisor that hosts the TVM.
CKID memory encryption key configured for use with TEE data.
Physical port that can be an upstream switch port, or an Endpoint port, or an RCD Upstream Port.
Universally Unique IDentifier as defined in the IETF RFC 4122 Specification
Virtual CXL Switch. Includes entities within the physical switch belonging to a single VH. It is identified using the VCS ID.
Downstream vPPB in a Host ES that is bound to one vUSP within a specific Downstream ES.
Virtual Hierarchy. Everything from the CXL RP down, including the CXL RP, CXL PPBs, and CXL Endpoints. Hierarchy ID means the same as PCIe.
A mode of operation where CXL RP is the root of the hierarchy
Virtual PCI-to-PCI Bridge inside a CXL switch that is host-owned. Can be bound to a port that is either disconnected, connected to a PCIe component or connected to a CXL component.
Upstream vPPB in a Downstream ES that is bound to one vDSP within a specific Host ES.
As defined in PCIe Base Specification
Extended System Description Table as defined in ACPI Specification
